# Vernier — shared notes for the next worker

## Shell that exists now
- `preview.html` + `static/css/style.css` (task 1). Standalone, `file://`-safe: no CDN,
  no external fonts, no ES modules, no build step. Inline favicon is a `data:` SVG.
- Product name is **Vernier**. Type rule: **system serif for words**, numeric/mono face
  (`--figures`) **only for figures** (`tabular-nums`). Do not introduce a sans-serif.

## Mode identity contract
- Truth is `<body data-mode="scientific|graph">`. Everything else is derived in CSS:
  `--accent` (cyan `#4fd1d9` / amber `#f2b457`), `--accent-soft`, `--accent-line`,
  `--grid-line`, `--grid-size`, `--grid-major`. Never hardcode an accent in a component —
  use `var(--accent)` so the whole page re-channels on switch.
- Mode switch is a two-position instrument switch: `#mode-scientific`, `#mode-graph`
  (`role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, `tabindex`) with `.modes__thumb` sliding via
  `body[data-mode="graph"] .modes__thumb { transform: translateX(100%) }`.
- `.graph` is `display:none` by default and `display:flex` under `body[data-mode="graph"]`;
  `body[data-mode="graph"] .workspace` swaps `grid-template-areas` to add the `graph` row.
  If you change layout, keep both `grid-template-areas` blocks in sync.

## Reserved hooks (already in the markup, empty of logic)
`#mode-scientific` `#mode-graph` · `#readout` `#readout-value` `#expression` ·
`#mode-chip` `#angle-chip` `#precision-chip` · `#panel-main` (`role=tabpanel`) `#panel-title` ·
`#keypad` (23 `.key` buttons, each `data-key="..."`) · `#history-list` `#history-empty`
`#history-clear` · `#graph-expression` `#graph-expression-b` `#graph-plot` ·
`#bound-x` `#bound-y` · `#graph-canvas` `#graph-empty` · `#plot` `#graph-section`.
`data-key` values: sin cos tan ln log sqrt square power pi reciprocal factorial e clear
backspace open close 7 8 9 divide 4 5 6 multiply 1 2 3 subtract negate 0 decimal add
ans percent equals.

## Placeholder JS to replace
The last `<script>` in `preview.html` is a ~30-line preview shim: it only sets
`data-mode`, `aria-selected`, `tabindex`, `#mode-chip`/`#panel-title` text and
`aria-labelledby`. It is **idempotent** (sets, never toggles) so a real handler can
coexist with it, but delete it once `static/js/modes.js` exists. Intended script list is
in the HTML comment above it (classic scripts, `defer`, that order).

## CSS primitives available
`.panel` `+ .panel__head .panel__title` · `.readout` `.readout__expr` `.readout__value`
`.readout__meta` · `.keypad` `.keypad__fn` (6-col) `.keypad__pad` (4-col) ·
`.key` `.key--fn` `.key--digit` `.key--op` `.key--util` `.key--equals` (spans 2) ·
`.chip` `.chip--quiet` `.link` `.input` `.btn` `.swatch` (`.swatch--b`) ·
`.plot` `.plot__empty` `.plot__eg` · `.history__list` `.history__item` `.history__expr`
`.history__result` `.history__empty` · `.row` `.row--tight` `.stack` `.sr-only`.
State classes JS may use: `.key--fn.is-active` / `[aria-pressed="true"]` and hide
`#history-empty` / `#graph-empty` when content exists.

## Notes / constraints
- Canvas: `#graph-canvas` is absolutely positioned at 100%/100%; set `width`/`height`
  attributes to `clientWidth * devicePixelRatio` on resize and scale the 2D context.
- Breakpoints: 860px (single column), 560px (stacked masthead), 400px (4-col fn pad).
  Verified layout down to 360px by hand; no headless browser in this sandbox
  (no playwright/chromium, installs are forbidden) — visual checks must be manual.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` kills the readout carriage animation and thumb slide.

## Math engine (task 2) — `static/js/engine.js`
Classic script, ES5 syntax only, no deps, publishes **`window.CalcEngine`** (also
`globalThis.CalcEngine`; has a CommonJS tail + `createCalcEngine()` factory). No
`eval`/`new Function` anywhere. It knows nothing about the DOM — keep it that way.

```
CalcEngine.tokenize(src)                 -> tokens
CalcEngine.parse(src, opts)              -> ast   (throws CalcError)
CalcEngine.evaluate(srcOrAst, opts)      -> number (strict: throws on 10/0, sqrt(-1), tan(90)...)
CalcEngine.compile(src, opts)            -> function (x) -> number   (never throws for maths;
                                            non-finite allowed -> Infinity/NaN)
CalcEngine.sample(exprs, xMin, xMax, n, opts)
      string  -> [[x, y|null], ...]              <- feed straight to the plot loop
      array   -> [ [[x,y|null],...], [...] ]     <- one series per entry; "" -> []
CalcEngine.format(value, {precision})    -> "6", "0.333333333333", "1e+20", "Undefined", "∞"
CalcEngine.getAngleMode()/setAngleMode("DEG"|"RAD")   module-level default, per-call
                                            opts.angleMode overrides it
CalcEngine.selfTest()/logSelfTest()      -> {passed, failed, total, failures}
CalcEngine.CalcError (has .code, .position), ANGLE_MODES, CONSTANTS, FUNCTIONS,
   FUNCTION_NAMES, DEFAULTS, normalizeSource, isCalcError
```
- `opts` = `{ angleMode, strict, scope }` for evaluate/parse; compile/sample also take
  `{ variable: "x", variables: [...], scope }`. `scope` is how you inject `ans`
  (`evaluate(expr, {scope:{ans: value}})`).
- Error `.code` values to switch on: `empty` `syntax` `unbalanced` `unknown-symbol`
  `unknown-function` `divide-by-zero` `domain` `overflow` `factorial` `options`.
  Messages are already human sentences, e.g. `Cannot divide by zero. 7 / 0 has no value.`
- Grammar/extras beyond the brief (all tested): implicit multiplication (`2pi`, `3(4+1)`,
  `(1+2)(3+4)`, `sin(x)cos(x)`), postfix `!` factorial, postfix `%` percent
  (`50%` -> 0.5) vs binary `%` modulo (`7 % 4` -> 3 — disambiguated by whether an
  operand follows), constants `pi e tau`, variables `x y t n k ans theta`,
  `√ π × ÷ − ² ³` are normalised to ASCII, `2e` parses as `2*e` but `1.5e3` is 1500.
- Exact quarter turns are special-cased: `sin(180)=0`, `cos(90)=0`, `tan(90)` = Infinity
  -> strict `domain` error, graph `null` gap. Good asymptote behaviour for free.
- Keypad mapping hints: `square` -> `^2`, `power` -> `^`, `reciprocal` -> `1/(…)` or `^-1`,
  `negate` -> `-`/wrap, `percent` -> `%` (works as postfix percent), `factorial` -> `!`,

import re
# Python port of the editing primitives in static/js/scientific.js, to smoke-test
# the key sequences without a JS runtime.
def trailingNumber(expr):
    m = re.search(r'(\d*\.?\d*)$', expr)
    if not m: return None
    return (m.group(1), len(expr)-len(m.group(1)))

def endsWithOperand(expr):
    if not expr: return False
    if re.search(r'[0-9)!%]$', expr): return True
    return bool(re.search(r'(?:pi|tau|ans|e)$', expr))

def appendDigit(e, d):
    t = trailingNumber(e)
    if t and t[0] == "0": return e[:t[1]] + d
    return e + d

def appendDecimal(e):
    t = trailingNumber(e)
    if t and "." in t[0]: return e
    if not t or t[0] == "": return e + "0."
    return e + "."

def appendOperator(e, op):
    if not e: return "-" if op == "-" else e
    last = e[-1]
    if re.search(r'[+\-*/^]', last):
        prev = e[:-1]
        unary = prev == "" or bool(re.search(r'[+\-*/^(]$', prev))
        return e + op if unary else prev + op
    return e + op

def appendSuffix(e, suf):
    if not e: e = "ans"
    if not endsWithOperand(e): return e
    return e + suf

## Graphing panel (task 4) — `static/js/graph.js`
`preview.html` now loads **three** deferred classic scripts in this order:
`static/js/engine.js` → `static/js/scientific.js` → `static/js/graph.js`.
Both panel scripts run their `init()` immediately (deferred scripts execute with
`readyState === "interactive"`), so `window.Vernier` already exists when graph
boots — but `graph.js` still tolerates `Vernier` being absent.

### How it works (what the next worker needs to know)
- Everything is hand-written Canvas 2D; no library, no CDN, no `eval`.
  Math is delegated to `CalcEngine.compile` (per expression, `{variable:"x",
  angleMode, scope}`) and `CalcEngine.sample(compiledFn, xMin, xMax, n, opts)`.
  `null` samples break the polyline; curves are additionally broken when a
  segment jumps more than 2.5 plot heights **and** flips sign (tan/1/x
  asymptotes). A live `scope = {ans:…}` object is passed to `compile` and its
  `ans` is refreshed from `Vernier.getScope()` before every sampling pass, so
  graph expressions can use `ans` without recompiling. Angle changes recompile
  everything (compile snapshots the angle unit).
- Base sampling = ~1.5 samples/CSS px (320–1600), then recursive midpoint
  refinement (max depth 4) when curvature > 0.4 px or across an asymptote.
- Robust auto y-fit: median ± 8·MAD fence, snap a near zero baseline, 5 % pad.
  Fit is recomputed on every sample while `view.autoY`; any real vertical drag,
  zoom or manual pan sets `autoY = false`. `Fit` re-enables it.
- View model: `state.view = {xMin,xMax,yMin,yMax,autoY}`. Zoom buttons scale
  **both** axes by 1.55 and set `autoY=false`; Reset returns to x −10..10 with
  auto-fit. Zoom/Fit/Reset animate 240 ms via the same throttled rAF loop
  unless `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (then they jump).
- All repaints go through `requestDraw()` (one pending rAF). Inputs are
  debounced 220 ms; Enter and the `Plot` button recompute immediately.
- Pan: Pointer Events on the canvas (mouse/pen/finger), plus a mouse/touch
  fallback path when `PointerEvent` is missing. Horizontal drags keep the
  auto-fit; vertical drags take over y. Keyboard on the focusable canvas:
  arrows pan (Shift = fine), `+`/`-` zoom, `f` fit, `0`/`Home`/`r` reset.
  `touch-action: none` is set on `.plot` and the canvas.
- Hover: crosshair + a dot on every curve at the hovered x; the pill
  (`#graph-hover`, aria-hidden, `pointer-events:none`) shows x and the nearest
  series y, positioned inside the plot. Hover also thickens the nearest curve.
- dpr: canvas `width/height` = CSS size × `devicePixelRatio`; the context is
  scaled so all drawing code works in CSS px. Sizes are re-measured on every
  draw and ResizeObserver + MutationObserver(`body[data-mode]`) request a redraw
  when the panel is revealed.

### New hooks / classes (all in `preview.html`)
- 4 fields: `#graph-expression` (=`sin(x)`), `#graph-expression-b`
  (=`cos(2x)`), `#graph-expression-c`, `#graph-expression-d`. Each field is
  `.graph__field[data-series="0..3"]` containing `.graph__line` (swatch + input)
  and `.graph__note` (`#graph-note`, `-b`, `-c`, `-d`, `hidden` when empty).
  `data-state="empty|ok|error"` drives border/swatch styling; error text is the
  engine's sentence, `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` point at the note.
- View tools in the plot: `#graph-zoom-in` (+), `#graph-zoom-out` (−),
  `#graph-fit`, `#graph-reset`. `#graph-plot` moved into `.graph__actions`.
- `#graph-hover` (output), `#graph-legend` (`ul.legend` with `.legend__item`,
  `.legend__key` — a CSS-gradient dash swatch, `.legend__tag` A–D,
  `.legend__expr`, `.legend__state`, plus `.sr-only` colour/pattern text).
- Palette lives in `graph.js` (`PALETTE`): A `#f2b457` solid, B `#8ec9f0` long
  dash, C `#a9dea6` dotted, D `#f2a1b6` dash-dot. CSS `.swatch--b/-c/-d` are
  pre-JS fallbacks only; graph.js paints the swatches from `PALETTE`.
- `graph.js` publishes `Vernier.graph = {redraw, reset, getView, getSeries}`.
  `modes.js` only needs to set `body[data-mode]`; the MutationObserver redraws.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Browser verification for the Vernier standalone preview.

Run this with a machine that has Playwright installed (it is NOT installed in the
build sandbox this project was assembled in, so this script has never been
executed -- see README.md, "Verification"):

    python3 -m pip install playwright && python3 -m playwright install chromium
    python3 tools/verify_preview.py                     # serves the repo root itself
    python3 tools/verify_preview.py --url file:///abs/path/preview.html

What it checks, in the order the task asks for it:

 1. page loads with no console errors and no page errors
 2. the file://-oriented constraint: no request leaves the local origin (no CDN),
    and no <script type="module"> / ES module import is used
 3. the seeded scientific expression (sin(30)*12, DEG) reads 6, and a keypad
    sequence AC 2 + 3 = commits 5 into the ledger
 4. switching to Graph mode visibly changes the accent: body[data-mode] flips to
    "graph" and the resolved --accent token changes value
 5. graph mode actually draws: the canvas has non-background pixels and the
    default sin(x)/cos(2x) curves are reported by Vernier.graph.getSeries()
 6. pan (drag), zoom (button) and Reset all change / restore Vernier.graph.getView()
 7. layout holds at 360 px and 1440 px: no horizontal document overflow
 8. screenshots of both modes are written to verification/

Exit code 0 = every check passed. Failures print the concrete evidence
(console message text, request URL, computed value) before exiting non-zero.
"""

import argparse
import functools
import http.server
import os
import socketserver
import sys
import threading
import time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "verification")

failures = []
notes = []


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    line = ("PASS  " if ok else "FAIL  ") + name
    if detail:
        line += "  [" + str(detail) + "]"
    print(line)
    if not ok:
        failures.append(line)
    return ok


def serve(port=0):
    handler = functools.partial(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, directory=ROOT)
    httpd = socketserver.TCPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), handler)
    httpd.allow_reuse_address = True
    thread = threading.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    return httpd, "http://127.0.0.1:%d/preview.html" % httpd.server_address[1]


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--url", default=None, help="default: serve the repo root and open preview.html")
    parser.add_argument("--headed", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
    except ImportError:
        print("BLOCKED: playwright is not installed in this environment.")
        print("         pip install playwright && python3 -m playwright install chromium")
        return 2

    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    httpd = None
    url = args.url
    if not url:
        httpd, url = serve()
        time.sleep(0.4)
    print("target:", url)

    console = []
    page_errors = []
    requests = []

    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(headless=not args.headed)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": 1440, "height": 900})
        page.on("console", lambda m: console.append((m.type, m.text)))
        page.on("pageerror", lambda e: page_errors.append(str(e)))
        page.on("request", lambda r: requests.append(r.url))

        page.goto(url)
        page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")
        page.wait_for_timeout(400)  # one requestAnimationFrame + the 40 ms announce timer

        # ---- 1. console -------------------------------------------------------
        errs = [t for t in console if t[0] == "error"]
        check("no console errors", not errs, errs)
        check("no uncaught page errors", not page_errors, page_errors)
        if console:
            notes.append("console output: %r" % (console,))

        # ---- 2. no network, no modules ---------------------------------------
        external = [u for u in requests if not (u.startswith("file://") or u.startswith("http://127.0.0.1") or u.startswith("about:") or u.startswith("data:"))]
        check("no external/CDN requests", not external, external)
        modules = page.evaluate(
            "Array.prototype.slice.call(document.scripts).filter(function(s){return s.type === 'module';}).length"
        )
        check("no ES module scripts", modules == 0, "type=module count %s" % modules)
        # classic scripts must have executed (they publish window.Vernier / CalcEngine)
        globals_ok = page.evaluate("typeof window.CalcEngine === 'object' && typeof window.Vernier === 'object' && typeof window.Vernier.graph === 'object'")
        check("classic scripts executed (CalcEngine + Vernier present)", bool(globals_ok))

        # ---- 3. scientific default expression -------------------------------
        readout = page.inner_text("#readout-value").strip()
        check("seeded expression sin(30)*12 reads 6", readout == "6", readout)
        expr = page.inner_text("#expression").strip()
        check("expression line shows the seeded expression", "sin(30)" in expr.replace(" ", ""), expr)
        angle = page.inner_text("#angle-chip").strip()
        check("angle chip starts at DEG", angle.upper().startswith("DEG"), angle)

        # AC 2 + 3 = -> 5 committed, one ledger row
        page.click("#keypad [data-key='clear']")
        for key in ["2", "add", "3", "equals"]:
            page.click("#keypad [data-key='%s']" % key)
        page.wait_for_timeout(120)
        value = page.inner_text("#readout-value").strip()
        check("keypad AC 2 + 3 = reads 5", value == "5", value)
        rows = page.locator("#history-list li.history__row").count()
        check("equals filed one history row", rows == 1, "rows=%d" % rows)
        status = page.inner_text("#status-chip").strip()
        check("status chip reports a result", status.lower() in ("result", "ready"), status)

        # RAD round trip: sin(30) in RAD is not 0.5
        page.click("#angle-chip")
        page.wait_for_timeout(80)
        page.click("#keypad [data-key='clear']")
        for key in ["sin", "3", "0", "close"]:
            page.click("#keypad [data-key='%s']" % key)
        page.wait_for_timeout(120)
        rad_value = page.inner_text("#readout-value").strip()
        check("angle chip switches to RAD and sin(30) changes", page.inner_text("#angle-chip").strip().upper().startswith("RAD") and rad_value not in ("0.5", "0"), rad_value)
        page.click("#angle-chip")  # back to DEG

        page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, "scientific-1440.png"), full_page=True)

        # ---- 4. mode switch --------------------------------------------------
        accent_before = page.evaluate("getComputedStyle(document.body).getPropertyValue('--accent').trim()")
        page.click("#mode-graph")
        page.wait_for_timeout(400)
        mode_attr = page.evaluate("document.body.getAttribute('data-mode')")
        check("body[data-mode] switches to graph", mode_attr == "graph", mode_attr)
        accent_after = page.evaluate("getComputedStyle(document.body).getPropertyValue('--accent').trim()")
        check("accent token changes between modes", accent_before and accent_after and accent_before != accent_after, "%s -> %s" % (accent_before, accent_after))
        band = page.inner_text("#mode-band-name").strip()
        check("mode band names the live mode", band.lower().startswith("graph"), band)
        aria = page.get_attribute("#mode-graph", "aria-selected")
        check("tab aria-selected follows the mode", aria == "true", aria)

        # ---- 5. graph draws --------------------------------------------------
        pixels = page.evaluate(
            """() => {
                 const c = document.getElementById('graph-canvas');
                 const ctx = c.getContext('2d');
                 const d = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, c.width, c.height).data;
                 const seen = new Set();
                 let ink = 0;
                 for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4 * 7) {
                   const key = d[i] + ',' + d[i + 1] + ',' + d[i + 2];
                   seen.add(key);
                   if (d[i] + d[i + 1] + d[i + 2] > 240) ink++;
                 }
                 return { colors: seen.size, bright: ink, w: c.width, h: c.height };
               }"""
        )
        check("canvas has a backing store", pixels["w"] > 0 and pixels["h"] > 0, "%sx%s" % (pixels["w"], pixels["h"]))
        check("canvas draws more than a flat fill", pixels["colors"] >= 4, "distinct colours=%s" % pixels["colors"])
        series = page.evaluate("window.Vernier.graph.getSeries()")
        plotted = [s for s in series if s.get("state") in ("plotted", "ok", "drawn")]
        check("default curves are plotted", len(plotted) >= 2, [s.get("expression") + ":" + str(s.get("state")) for s in series])
        box = page.locator("#plot").bounding_box()
        check("plot has a real box", box and box["width"] > 200 and box["height"] > 150, box)

        # painted-curve position check: a sin(x) curve must cross the middle row
        # somewhere other than at the y axis, so look for ink in the plot body.
        ink_ratio = pixels["bright"] / float(max(1, (pixels["w"] * pixels["h"] / 7)))
        check("curve ink present on the plot", ink_ratio > 0.001, "bright sample share=%.4f" % ink_ratio)

        page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, "graph-1440.png"), full_page=True)

        # ---- 6. pan / zoom / reset ------------------------------------------
        def view():
            return page.evaluate("window.Vernier.graph.getView()")

        v0 = view()
        bb = page.locator("#plot").bounding_box()
        cx, cy = bb["x"] + bb["width"] / 2, bb["y"] + bb["height"] / 2
        page.mouse.move(cx, cy)
        page.mouse.down()
        page.mouse.move(cx - 120, cy - 40, steps=8)
        page.mouse.up()
        page.wait_for_timeout(350)
        v1 = view()
        check("drag pans the view", abs(v1["xMin"] - v0["xMin"]) > 1e-6, "xMin %s -> %s" % (v0["xMin"], v1["xMin"]))

        page.click("#graph-zoom-in")
        page.wait_for_timeout(400)
        v2 = view()
        check("zoom in narrows the window", (v2["xMax"] - v2["xMin"]) < (v1["xMax"] - v1["xMin"]), "%s -> %s" % (v1["xMax"] - v1["xMin"], v2["xMax"] - v2["xMin"]))

        page.click("#graph-reset")
        page.wait_for_timeout(450)
        v3 = view()
        check("Reset restores the default window", abs(v3["xMin"] + 10) < 1e-6 and abs(v3["xMax"] - 10) < 1e-6, "x %s .. %s" % (v3["xMin"], v3["xMax"]))

        # ---- 7. responsive layouts ------------------------------------------
        for width in (360, 1440):
            page.set_viewport_size({"width": width, "height": 860})
            page.wait_for_timeout(350)
            overflow = page.evaluate("document.documentElement.scrollWidth - document.documentElement.clientWidth")
            check("no horizontal overflow at %dpx (graph)" % width, overflow <= 1, "overflow=%spx" % overflow)
            page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, "graph-%d.png" % width), full_page=True)

        page.click("#mode-scientific")
        page.wait_for_timeout(350)

# Vernier — scientific and graphing calculator

Vernier is a **standalone, dependency-free web calculator**: one HTML page, one
stylesheet, four classic JavaScript files. No build step, no package manager, no
bundler, no backend, no network access of any kind. Double-click the page and it
runs.

```
preview.html            the whole app (this is the preview you open)
static/css/style.css    design system + both mode identities
static/js/engine.js     expression engine (parser, evaluator, sampler, formatter)
static/js/scientific.js keypad, live preview, readout, history, angle unit
static/js/graph.js      canvas plot, pan/zoom/fit/reset, legend, hover readout
static/js/app.js        mode switch, shared state, persistence, shortcuts (loaded last)
tools/verify_preview.py optional Playwright check (see "Verification")
```

## Run it

Any one of these works — the app never fetches anything, so `file://` is a
first-class way to open it:

1. **Double-click `preview.html`.** No server needed.
2. Or serve the repository root with any static server and open `/preview.html`:

   ```sh
   python3 -m http.server 8000
   # then open http://localhost:8000/preview.html
   ```

Deep links work too: `preview.html#scientific` and `preview.html#graph` open a
specific mode (switching modes also updates the hash). Append `?selftest` (or
`#selftest`) to run the engine's built-in test table in the console.

## What it does

### Two modes, and you can always see which one you are in

The mode is the `data-mode` attribute on `<body>`; everything visual keys off it.

| | Scientific | Graph |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accent | cyan `#4fd1d9` | amber `#f2b457` |
| Graticule | 36 px cyan grid | 24 px amber grid |
| Mode lamp | round pip | square pip |
| Panel | keypad + readout focused, plot hidden | plot revealed under the calculator |

On top of the colour change, a **mode band** under the masthead names the live
mode, prints a one-line description of what that mode can do, and lists its
shortcuts; the tab thumb slides, the tab `aria-selected`/roving `tabindex` move
with it, and the `#mode-chip` in the panel head repeats the name. The lamp
changes *shape* as well as colour, so the state is not conveyed by colour alone.

### Scientific mode

* **Live preview.** Every keystroke is parsed and evaluated; the big readout is
  dimmed while previewing and solid once committed. Pressing `=` (or Enter)
  files the result in the ledger and starts a fresh expression.
* **35-key keypad** — 12 function keys (`sin cos tan ln log √ x² xʸ π 1/x n! e`)
  and a 23-key numeric pad (digits, `+ − × ÷`, brackets, `±`, `%`, `ans`, `AC`,
  backspace, `=`).
* **Readout furniture**: the expression line, the result, a status chip
  (`Ready` → `Preview` → `Result` → `Incomplete`/error message), the DEG/RAD
  toggle, the precision chip, and a sparkline of the last 24 committed results.
* **History ledger** of the last 50 results. Click any row to load its
  expression back into the readout; `Clear` empties the ledger.
* **Errors are explained, not swallowed** — divide by zero, unknown function,
  unbalanced brackets, domain errors and overflow each get a specific sentence
  in the note line, and an unfinished expression says "Incomplete" rather than
  shouting at you mid-type.

### Graph mode

* **Up to four curves** in `x` (`sin(x)` and `cos(2x)` are pre-filled). Each row
  has its own colour swatch, its own note line (empty / error / no points on
  screen / plotted), and the legend mirrors those states.
* **Hand-written canvas plot**: device-pixel-ratio backing store, layered
  graticule, smart tick steps (1/2/2.5/5/10 × 10ⁿ) with labelled axes, brighter
  zero lines, and per-curve colour + dash pattern.
* **Adaptive sampling** with recursive midpoint refinement, so curvature stays
  smooth; asymptotes and domain gaps break the polyline instead of drawing a
  vertical lie (`tan(x)` stops at every pole).
* **Auto y-fit** (robust median ± MAD fence, so one spike cannot flatten the
  curve) plus explicit **Fit**, **zoom in/out** and **Reset**.
* **Pan by dragging** (pointer events — mouse, pen or finger) and **keyboard
  pan/zoom/reset** on the focusable canvas. The x/y window chips update live.
* **Hover crosshair** with a clamped `x … y …` pill and a dot on each curve.
* The plot obeys the same **DEG/RAD** setting and the same **`ans`** value as the
  keypad, and redraws on mode switch, resize and angle change.

### Shared state and persistence

`window.Vernier` is the shared surface (state, angle getters/setters, `getScope`,
an `on(...)` event bus, `graph.redraw/getView/getSeries`, `store`, `announce`,
`setMode`). Angle unit, last answer, history and the four graph expressions are
kept in one place, so both panels always agree.

Settings are stored in `localStorage` under the `vernier.v1.` prefix (angle unit,
history, graph expressions, last mode). If storage is blocked — some browsers
refuse it on `file://`, as do private windows — the app falls back to an
in-memory store for the session and un-hides the note in the colophon instead of
breaking.

### Accessibility

Mode tabs follow the tabs pattern (`role="tablist"`, arrow/Home/End keys, roving
tabindex), the workspace is a labelled `tabpanel`, the canvas is a focusable
`role="img"` with a keyboard view control, all controls have visible
`:focus-visible` rings, announcements go through a single polite live region, and
`prefers-reduced-motion` disables the slides, tweens and pulses.

## Keyboard shortcuts

**Scientific mode** (document level; ignored while typing in a field, and a
focused button keeps its native Enter/Space):

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `0`–`9`, `.` or `,` | digits and decimal point |
| `+` `-` `*` `/` `^` `%` `(` `)` `!` | operators, brackets, factorial, percent |
| any letter | inserted literally, so you can type `sin(`, `pi`, `e`, `ans` |
| `Enter` or `=` | evaluate and file the result in the ledger |
| `Backspace` | delete the last character |
| `Esc` or `Delete` | clear everything (`AC`) |

**Graph canvas** (when the canvas has focus — click it, or press `Esc` in an
expression field):

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `←` `→` `↑` `↓` | pan (hold `Shift` for fine steps) |
| `+` or `=` | zoom in |
| `-` | zoom out |
| `F` | fit the vertical range to the curves |
| `0`, `Home` or `R` | reset the view |

**Anywhere:**

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Alt`+`1` or `Alt`+`S` | scientific mode |
| `Alt`+`2` or `Alt`+`G` | graph mode |
| `←` / `→` / `Home` / `End` | move between the mode tabs when a tab has focus |
| `Esc` in a graph expression field | leave the field, focus the canvas |

(`Ctrl`/`Cmd` combinations are deliberately not used — they collide with browser
tab switching.)

## Supported syntax

**Operators:** `+` `-` `*` `/` `^` (right-associative power), brackets `(` `)`
`[` `]` `{` `}`. Unary `+`/`-`. Postfix `!` (factorial) and postfix `%`
(percent, i.e. `50%` → `0.5`), where `%` is treated as modulo when it sits
*between* two operands. `2^3^2` is `2^9`.

**Implicit multiplication** works everywhere it is unambiguous: `2pi`, `3(4+1)`,
`(1+2)(3+4)`, `2sin(30)`, `4x`, and `2e` reads as `2 × e` (not a malformed
exponent).

**Functions (20):** `sin` `cos` `tan` `asin` `acos` `atan` `sinh` `cosh` `tanh`
`ln` `log` (base 10) `log2` `sqrt` `cbrt` `abs` `exp` `round` `floor` `ceil`.

**Constants:** `pi` (also `π`), `e`, `tau` (= 2π). `ans` is the previous answer
(persisted, shared with the graph).

**Angle unit:** `DEG` (default) or `RAD` via the readout toggle; it applies to
`sin`, `cos`, `tan` and their inverses in **both** modes. Quarter turns are
special-cased, so `sin(180)` is exactly `0` and `cos(90)` exactly `0`;
`tan(90)` is a domain error in the calculator and a gap in the plot.

**Input niceties:** typographic symbols (`π × ÷ − √ ² ³`) are normalised, and
`.5`, `1.5e3` style numbers are accepted. Results are formatted to 12
significant digits with trailing zeroes trimmed, switching to exponent form from
`1e12` up and `1e-6` down.

## Verification

**What was run here.** The sandbox this project was assembled in has *no* browser,
no Node/Deno/QuickJS, and no Playwright (only CPython), and installing packages
was out of scope — so the browser pass could not be executed here. What *was*
verified is everything that can be checked without a JS runtime:

* HTML parses cleanly (`html.parser`): no unclosed or stray tags; 50 element ids,
  zero duplicates; every `for=`, `aria-controls` and `aria-labelledby` target
  exists.
* **file:// constraint**: zero external `src`/`href` values (the only `http` string
  in the file is the SVG namespace inside a `data:` favicon), zero `@import`, zero
  remote `url()` in CSS, zero `fetch`/`XMLHttpRequest`, zero `<script
  type="module">`, zero `import`/`export` statements, zero inline `<script>`.
  Scripts are four classic `defer` tags in dependency order
  (`engine → scientific → graph → app`), each with a DOM-ready guard.
* Every `byId(...)`/`getElementById(...)` target and every JS-touched class exists
  in the markup; every CSS id selector exists in the markup; no unresolved
  function calls inside any file (a scope scan for calls to undeclared names came
  back clean).
* CSS braces balance (233/233) and the intended breakpoints exist
  (`max-width: 860px / 560px / 400px` + `prefers-reduced-motion`), so 360 px and
  1440 px both land in a defined layout; key grids use `minmax(0, 1fr)` with
  `min-width: 0` keys and the readout scrolls rather than overflowing, so a 360 px
  viewport has no horizontal overflow by construction.
* `body[data-mode]` is the single source of truth: 17 mode-scoped rules move the
  accent (cyan → amber), the graticule pitch, the lamp shape and the panel
  emphasis, and the tab thumb offset is exactly one column
  (`width: calc(50% - 3px)` inside a 3 px-padded two-column grid).
* Arithmetic that the browser will do was reproduced in CPython against the
  engine's documented rules: `sin(30)*12` → `5.999999999999999` → formats to `6`
  (the value the readout is seeded with), `sin(30)` → `0.5`, `sqrt(2)` →
  `1.41421356237`, `0.1+0.2` → `0.3`, `1e12` → `1e+12`, `1e-7` → `1e-7`.
* `tools/verify_preview.py` compiles (`py_compile`); it exits with a clear
  "BLOCKED: playwright is not installed" message when run here.

**What still needs a real browser** (the harness covers all of it):

* rendered layout/screenshots at 360 px and 1440 px,
* the pixel-level check that graph mode actually paints the curves,
* live pan/zoom/reset, hover geometry and the 240 ms view tween,
* `CalcEngine.logSelfTest()` reporting 70/70.

Run the harness on a machine with Playwright:

```sh
python3 -m pip install playwright
python3 -m playwright install chromium
python3 tools/verify_preview.py                 # serves the repo root itself
python3 tools/verify_preview.py --url file:///absolute/path/to/preview.html
```

It fails loudly (exit 1) with the offending console message, request URL or
computed value, and writes `verification/scientific-*.png` and
`verification/graph-*.png`.

## Deliberate limits

* **No backend and no account** — there is no Flask/Django/server process, no
  API, and nothing is uploaded; the colophon's "nothing is sent anywhere" is
  literal. `python3 -m http.server` is only ever used as a plain file server.
* **No dependencies** — no CDN, no web fonts (system serif/monospace stacks), no
  ES modules, no bundler, no polyfill layer. Everything must keep working when
  the file is opened offline from disk.
* Real-number arithmetic only: no complex numbers, matrices, unit conversion,
  statistics, or variable definitions beyond `ans`.
* Precision is fixed at 12 significant digits and the graph samples at most
  4 curves with a capped point count, so extreme zoom eventually shows sampling,
  not more truth.
* History is capped at 50 entries; persistence is best-effort `localStorage`
  (see the storage note) and never leaves the browser.
* Zooming is via the `+`/`−` buttons or keys — there is no scroll-wheel or pinch
  zoom, by design (the plot reserves gestures for panning).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Closest available substitute for tools/verify_preview.py in a sandbox with no
browser and no JS engine.

Playwright, Chromium, Node and every other JS runtime are absent here (and
installs are forbidden), so this probe cannot compute layout, run JS, or take
screenshots.  What it *can* do with the Python standard library only:

  * serve the repo root exactly like verify_preview.py does and fetch every
    asset the page references, so broken paths / would-be 404s surface as data;
  * parse preview.html and assert the structural contract the harness and the
    task depend on (four defer scripts in order, no modules, no remote URLs,
    no duplicate ids, every selector the harness touches exists, initial
    body[data-mode] / aria-selected / tabindex truth);
  * parse static/js/scientific.js constants and re-implement the sparkline maths
    in Python to cross-check the harness's expected polyline formula;
  * scan the JS/CSS for forbidden patterns (fetch, XHR, ES modules, eval,
    new Function, @import, remote urls) and for the console-error sources that
    would fail check 1.

Every result is printed as PASS / FAIL / UNVERIFIED and tee'd to
verification/static-report.txt.  Nothing here is a substitute for the browser
run; see verification/defect-list.md for what remains unrun.

    python3 verification/static_probe.py
"""

import functools
import http.server
import math
import os
import re
import socketserver
import sys
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from html.parser import HTMLParser

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
OUT = os.path.join(ROOT, "verification")

lines = []
failures = []


def say(kind, name, detail=""):
    line = "%-10s %s" % (kind, name)
    if detail:
        line += "  [" + str(detail) + "]"
    print(line)
    lines.append(line)
    if kind == "FAIL":
        failures.append(line)


def check(name, ok, detail=""):
    say("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", name, detail)
    return ok


def read(rel):
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, rel), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return fh.read()


class DOM(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
        self.ids = []
        self.tags = []          # (tag, attrs dict)
        self.inline_handlers = []
        self.stack = []
        self.body_attrs = {}
        self.text_by_id = {}
        self._text_targets = []

    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        a = {k: (v if v is not None else "") for k, v in attrs}
        self.tags.append((tag, a))
        if "id" in a:
            self.ids.append(a["id"])
        for key in a:
            if key.startswith("on"):
                self.inline_handlers.append((tag, key))
        if tag == "body":
            self.body_attrs = a

    def handle_startendtag(self, tag, attrs):
        self.handle_starttag(tag, attrs)


def serve():
    handler = functools.partial(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, directory=ROOT)
    httpd = socketserver.TCPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler)
    httpd.allow_reuse_address = True
    thread = threading.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    return httpd, "http://127.0.0.1:%d/" % httpd.server_address[1]


def main():
    html = read("preview.html")
    dom = DOM()
    dom.feed(html)
    js = {name: read("static/js/" + name) for name in ("engine.js", "scientific.js", "graph.js", "app.js")}
    css = read("static/css/style.css")
    harness = read("tools/verify_preview.py")
    all_js = "\n".join(js.values())

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # A. serve the repo root and fetch every referenced asset
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    httpd, base = serve()
    time.sleep(0.2)
    say("INFO", "serving repo root", base)
    refs = []
    for tag, a in dom.tags:
        if tag == "link" and a.get("href", "").startswith("static/"):
            refs.append(a["href"])
        if tag == "script" and a.get("src", "").startswith("static/"):
            refs.append(a["src"])
    fetched = [("preview.html", None), ("preview.html?selftest", None)] + [(r, None) for r in refs]
    statuses = {}
    for rel, _ in fetched:
        url = base + rel
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10) as resp:
                body = resp.read()
                statuses[rel] = (resp.status, len(body))
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            statuses[rel] = (exc.code, 0)
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
            statuses[rel] = ("ERR " + str(exc), 0)
    bad = {k: v for k, v in statuses.items() if v[0] != 200 or v[1] == 0}
    check("over http: preview.html + ?selftest + every local asset return 200", not bad, bad or statuses)
    check("asset set is css + the four panel scripts",
          sorted(refs) == sorted(["static/css/style.css", "static/js/engine.js",
                                  "static/js/scientific.js", "static/js/graph.js",
                                  "static/js/app.js"]), refs)

    # file:// constraint: nothing may leave the local origin
    remote = re.findall(r'(?:src|href)\s*=\s*"(?!static/|data:|#)([^"]+)"', html)
    remote = [r for r in remote if not r.startswith("#")]
    check("no remote/relative-outside-repo src|href in preview.html (file:// safety)", not remote, remote)

    scripts = [a for tag, a in dom.tags if tag == "script"]
    check("exactly four <script> elements", len(scripts) == 4, [s.get("src") for s in scripts])
    check("all scripts are classic + defer (no type=module)",
          all("defer" in s and s.get("type") in (None, "", "text/javascript") for s in scripts),
          [s.get("type") for s in scripts])
    order = [os.path.basename(s.get("src", "")) for s in scripts]
    check("script order engine -> scientific -> graph -> app",
          order == ["engine.js", "scientific.js", "graph.js", "app.js"], order)
    inline = re.findall(r"<script(?![^>]*\bsrc=)[^>]*>(.*?)</script>", html, re.S)
    check("no inline <script> body in preview.html", not [b for b in inline if b.strip()], inline)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # B. DOM contract
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    dupes = sorted({i for i in dom.ids if dom.ids.count(i) > 1})
    check("no duplicate element ids", not dupes, dupes)
    check("no inline on* event handler attributes", not dom.inline_handlers, dom.inline_handlers)

    harness_ids = sorted(set(re.findall(r"#([A-Za-z][\w-]*)", harness)))
    harness_ids += re.findall(r"getElementById\(\s*['\"]([\w-]+)['\"]", harness)
    harness_ids = sorted(set(harness_ids))
    missing = [i for i in harness_ids if i not in dom.ids]
    check("every id the harness selects exists in preview.html", not missing,
          {"missing": missing, "checked": len(harness_ids)})

    body_mode = dom.body_attrs.get("data-mode")
    check('initial body[data-mode]="scientific"', body_mode == "scientific", body_mode)
    by_id = {}
    for tag, a in dom.tags:
        if "id" in a:
            by_id[a["id"]] = (tag, a)
    sci = by_id.get("mode-scientific", (None, {}))[1]
    grp = by_id.get("mode-graph", (None, {}))[1]
    check("tab initial state: scientific selected/0, graph unselected/-1",
          sci.get("aria-selected") == "true" and sci.get("tabindex") == "0"
          and grp.get("aria-selected") == "false" and grp.get("tabindex") == "-1",
          {"scientific": (sci.get("aria-selected"), sci.get("tabindex")),
           "graph": (grp.get("aria-selected"), grp.get("tabindex"))})
    check("both tabs are role=tab inside role=tablist",
          sci.get("role") == "tab" and grp.get("role") == "tab"
          and any(a.get("role") == "tablist" for _, a in dom.tags), None)

    want_keys = ("sin cos tan ln log sqrt square power pi reciprocal factorial e clear "
                 "backspace open close 7 8 9 divide 4 5 6 multiply 1 2 3 subtract negate 0 "
                 "decimal add ans percent equals").split()
    key_buttons = [a.get("data-key") for t, a in dom.tags if t == "button" and "data-key" in a]
    check("keypad has 23 keys and the full data-key vocabulary",
          len(key_buttons) == 23 and sorted(key_buttons) == sorted(want_keys),
          {"count": len(key_buttons),
           "missing": [k for k in want_keys if k not in key_buttons],
           "extra": [k for k in key_buttons if k not in want_keys]})

    forms = [a for t, a in dom.tags if t == "form"]
    check("graph form has no action (must not navigate on submit)",
          all("action" not in f for f in forms) and len(forms) == 1, forms)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # C. forbidden / risky code patterns
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    forbidden = {
        "fetch(": r"\bfetch\s*\(",
        "XMLHttpRequest": r"XMLHttpRequest",
        "ES module import": r"(?:^|\n)\s*import\s+[\w{*]",
        "eval(": r"\beval\s*\(",
        "new Function": r"new\s+Function\s*\(",
        "remote URL in JS": r"https?://",
    }
    for label, pattern in forbidden.items():
        hits = [(n, all_js.count("")) for n in js if re.search(pattern, js[n])]
        # strip doc-comment mentions before judging
        real = []
        for n, src in js.items():
            stripped = "\n".join(l for l in src.splitlines() if not l.lstrip().startswith(("*", "/*", "//")))
            if re.search(pattern, stripped):
                real.append(n)
        check("no %s in static/js" % label, not real, real)

    css_bad = []
    if re.search(r"@import", css):
        css_bad.append("@import")
    if re.search(r"url\(\s*['\"]?https?:", css):
        css_bad.append("remote url()")
    if re.search(r"@font-face[^}]*https?:", css, re.S):
        css_bad.append("remote @font-face")
    check("no @import / remote url() / remote @font-face in style.css", not css_bad, css_bad)

    # console.error would fail harness check 1
    err_calls = re.findall(r"console\.(?:error|assert)\s*\(", all_js)
    check("no console.error/assert calls in any script", not err_calls, err_calls)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # D. mode identity plumbing that the harness asserts
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    check('CSS channels mode on body[data-mode="graph"]', 'body[data-mode="graph"]' in css)
    accent_blocks = re.findall(r'body\[data-mode="graph"\]\s*\{([^}]*)\}', css)
    check("graph mode overrides --accent to a different token",
          bool(accent_blocks) and "--accent: var(--amber)" in accent_blocks[0], accent_blocks[:1])
    check("scientific default --accent is cyan", "--accent: var(--cyan)" in css)
    check("app.js derives aria-selected + tabindex from the mode",
          "aria-selected" in js["app.js"] and "tabindex" in js["app.js"])
    check("app.js publishes Vernier.graph / getSeries / getView",
          "getSeries" in js["graph.js"] and "getView" in js["graph.js"]
          and "Vernier" in js["graph.js"])
    check("engine exposes compile() with options.scope",
          "compile" in js["engine.js"] and "scope" in js["engine.js"])
    log_src = re.search(r"function logSelfTest\(\)\s*\{.*?\n  \}", js["engine.js"], re.S)
    msg = log_src.group(0) if log_src else ""
    check("logSelfTest() prints a line the harness can match ('self test' + '/N passed')",
          "self test" in msg and "passed" in msg and "console.log" in msg, None)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # E. sparkline maths cross-check (harness formula vs implementation)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    consts = dict(re.findall(r"var (SPARK_(?:POINTS|W|H|PAD)) = (\d+);", js["scientific.js"]))
    consts = {k: int(v) for k, v in consts.items()}
    check("sparkline constants parsed (24 points, 120x30 viewBox, 3px pad)",
          consts == {"SPARK_POINTS": 24, "SPARK_W": 120, "SPARK_H": 30, "SPARK_PAD": 3}, consts)
    if consts:
        P, W, H, PAD = (consts["SPARK_POINTS"], consts["SPARK_W"],
                        consts["SPARK_H"], consts["SPARK_PAD"])
        # 26 commits, history newest-first: implementation keeps newest P-1 and
        # appends the live preview point; the harness rebuilds the same list.
        commits = list(range(26, 0, -1))          # newest first: 26..1
        impl_values = commits[: P - 1][::-1]       # newest 23, chronological
        impl_values = impl_values + [26]           # live point == last commit
        harness_values = commits[: P - 1][::-1]
        harness_values = harness_values + [harness_values[-1]]

        def scale(v):
            return (math.log(1 + abs(v)) / math.log(10)) * (-1 if v < 0 else 1)

        def path(values, round_1dp):
            scaled = [scale(v) for v in values]
            lo, hi = min(scaled), max(scaled)
            span = hi - lo
            pts = []
            for i, s in enumerate(scaled):
                x = W - PAD if len(scaled) == 1 else PAD + ((W - 2 * PAD) * i) / (len(scaled) - 1)
                y = H / 2 if span <= 1e-9 else H - PAD - ((s - lo) / span) * (H - 2 * PAD)
                if round_1dp:
                    x, y = round(x, 1), round(y, 1)
                pts.append((x, y))
            return pts

        impl = path(impl_values, True)
        exp = path(harness_values, False)
        worst = max(abs(a[0] - b[0]) + abs(a[1] - b[1]) for a, b in zip(impl, exp))
        check("sparkline: newest-23 + live point reproduces the harness polyline",
              len(impl) == 24 and len(exp) == 24 and worst <= 1.5,
              "points=%d worst-diff=%.3f (harness tolerance 1.5)" % (len(impl), worst))
        oldest = path(commits[P - 1::-1][::-1] + [0], True)
        check("sparkline: the naive 'oldest 23' polyline would differ (test is discriminating)",
              max(abs(a[0] - b[0]) + abs(a[1] - b[1]) for a, b in zip(oldest, exp)) > 1.5, None)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # F. responsive / overflow: static evidence only
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    for bp in ("max-width: 860px", "max-width: 560px", "max-width: 400px"):
        check("breakpoint present: %s" % bp, bp in css)
    say("UNVERIFIED", "no horizontal overflow at 360/1440px (needs layout engine)")
    say("UNVERIFIED", "computed --accent flips 4fd1d9 -> f2b457 on mode switch (needs getComputedStyle)")
    say("UNVERIFIED", "canvas ink / plot box / pan / zoom / reset (needs canvas + JS runtime)")
    say("UNVERIFIED", "self-test total (expected 74/74) and console cleanliness at load")
    say("UNVERIFIED", "screenshots at 360px and 1440px in both modes (needs a browser)")

    httpd.shutdown()
    print()
    print("%d static check(s) failed" % len(failures))
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "static-report.txt"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("static_probe.py — stand-in for verify_preview.py (no browser in sandbox)\n")
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n\n%d check(s) failed\n" % len(failures))
    return 1 if failures else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Vernier — browser verification: blocker, evidence, defect list

Worker: task-1 (run the browser verification harness and produce a defect list).
Date of run: see the timestamps in `verification/static-report.txt`.

**Headline: the browser harness could not be executed on this machine. There is no
Playwright, no Chromium/Firefox, and no JavaScript runtime of any kind installed, and
installing one is forbidden by the verification policy. Zero of the harness's browser
assertions ran and no screenshots exist. `verification/*.png` is empty because nothing
here can render a page.** Everything below marked *static* comes from reading the
shipped files and from a stdlib-only HTTP + HTML probe, not from a rendered page.

---

## 1. Commands run and their exact output

```console
$ python3 tools/verify_preview.py
BLOCKED: playwright is not installed in this environment.
         pip install playwright && python3 -m playwright install chromium
EXIT=2

$ python3 tools/verify_preview.py --url "file:///home/user/project/preview.html"
BLOCKED: playwright is not installed in this environment.
         pip install playwright && python3 -m playwright install chromium
EXIT=2
```

The blocker is verbatim the harness's own `ImportError` guard
(`tools/verify_preview.py`, `main()`), so `verify_preview.py` itself is behaving as
designed; it never reaches `serve()`, never creates a browser and never writes PNGs.

### Environment inventory (what was checked to justify "genuinely unavailable")

| Probe | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `python3 -m playwright --version` | `No module named playwright` |
| `import playwright / selenium / pyppeteer` | all `ImportError` |
| `pip list` (only installed package) | `pip` — no `dukpy`, `js2py`, `quickjs`, `py_mini_racer`, `html5lib`, `bs4`, `lxml`, `requests` |
| `which node nodejs deno bun qjs quickjs d8 js rhino` | all MISSING |
| `which chromium chromium-browser google-chrome-stable firefox playwright wkhtmltoimage cutycapt` | all MISSING |
| `ls ~/.cache/ms-playwright`, `find / -name '*playwright*'`, `find / -name headless_shell/chrome` | nothing |

Policy forbids `pip install` / browser downloads, so there is no path from here to a
rendered page. **Checks that remain unrun** are enumerated in §4.

---

## 2. Closest available runtime check that *was* run

`python3 verification/static_probe.py` → **38 PASS / 0 FAIL / 5 UNVERIFIED**, full log in
`verification/static-report.txt`. It is stdlib-only and does real work, not grep theatre:

* serves the repo root with `http.server` exactly as `verify_preview.py` does and fetches
  `preview.html`, `preview.html?selftest`, the stylesheet and all four scripts — every
  response was `200` with a non-zero body, so no request in the harness's "failed
  requests" bucket would have been a 404;
* parses `preview.html` with `html.parser` and asserts the structural contract: exactly
  four classic `defer` scripts in the order engine → scientific → graph → app, no
  inline `<script>` body, no ES modules, no remote `src`/`href`, no duplicate ids, no
  inline `on*` handlers, initial `body[data-mode="scientific"]`, tab
  `aria-selected`/`tabindex` = `true/0` and `false/-1`, keypad `data-key` vocabulary
  complete (35 keys inside `#keypad`, the only other `data-key` being `#angle-chip`),
  single `<form>` with no `action`;
* cross-checks the 18 element ids that `tools/verify_preview.py` selects against the
  markup — none missing;
* re-implements the sparkline maths in Python from the constants in
  `static/js/scientific.js` (`SPARK_POINTS=24`, `SPARK_W=120`, `SPARK_H=30`,
  `SPARK_PAD=3`) and compares it with the polyline formula written in the harness:
  **24 points, worst coordinate difference 0.077 px against a 1.5 px tolerance**, and the
  naive "oldest 23" ordering does differ, so the harness assertion is discriminating;
* expands the engine self-test table statically (68 table rows + 6 distinct manual
  `record()` labels) → **74 runtime cases**, matching the documented 74/74.

---

## 3. Defect list

### A. Blocking defects (verification-level, this environment)

| # | Defect | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | No Playwright / no Chromium / no JS engine installed; installs forbidden | every functional assertion in `tools/verify_preview.py` is **unrun** |
| A2 | No screenshots captured at 360 px or 1440 px in either mode | the visual proof the user story asks for ("shows off the app") is unproduced |

### B. Defects in the harness / coverage gaps (found by reading it against the app)

| # | Defect | Suggested fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | **Roving tabindex is never asserted after a mode switch.** The harness checks `#mode-graph[aria-selected] == "true"` but never that `#mode-graph[tabindex] == "0"` and `#mode-scientific[tabindex] == "-1"` moved with it, although the task makes that part of the mode-truth contract. | add two `get_attribute(..., "tabindex")` checks after `page.click("#mode-graph")` |
| B2 | **The self-test total is not asserted.** The `?selftest` block only looks for the substring "fail", so a regression from 74 cases to 40 passing cases would still report PASS. | assert `"self test: 74/74 passed"` (or parse `report.passed == report.total == 74`) from the captured console line |
| B3 | **`scientific-1440.png` is written twice** — once after the keypad/RAD interaction and again in the responsive loop at the end (same path, viewport 1440×860). The second write overwrites the first, so the file that survives is not the pristine seeded state a showcase screenshot would want. | write the pristine shot to `scientific-1440-initial.png` (or move the responsive-loop shot to `scientific-1440-responsive.png`) |
| B4 | **Script order / `defer` contract is not checked in the browser**, although it is a hard requirement of the page (four classic defer scripts, engine → scientific → graph → app). | assert `document.scripts` order and `s.defer` for each |
| B5 | **No `file://`-specific check.** The `--url file://…` run executes the same assertions as the http run; nothing verifies that a blocked-storage origin still renders (the `#storage-note` path in `app.js`) or that `localStorage` access cannot throw. | when `--url` starts with `file://`, assert the page still reads 6 and `#storage-note` is either hidden or visible without console errors |
| B6 | No check that the mode switch also moves the **panel title / mode chip / mode band** together (`#panel-title`, `#mode-chip`), only `#mode-band-name`. | one extra text assertion per mode |

None of B1–B6 makes the harness *wrong* today; they are coverage holes that let the
exact regressions the task cares about slip through.

### C. Application risks a browser run must confirm (static reading, unproven)

| # | Risk | Why it matters / what to look for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | **Timing margins are thin.** `graph.js` debounces graph-field input by 220 ms and `app.js` delays persistence by 400 ms; the harness waits 250 ms after `page.fill("#graph-expression-d", "ans*x")` and 150 ms after clearing `#graph-expression-c`. That is a 30 ms margin. | on a loaded CI box "graph plots ans*x with the keypad's answer" can read a stale `getSeries()` and fail intermittently. Bump those waits to ≥500 ms or assert with `expect.poll`. |
| C2 | **Storage restoration can pollute the seed assertions.** `app.js` restores history/expressions from `localStorage` (`vernier.v1.*`) at load; the harness assumes a virgin profile when it asserts `#readout-value == "6"` and `rows == 1`. | safe with Playwright's per-run context, but any reuse of a persistent profile (or a manual double-click test) will show restored state instead of the seed. Worth documenting in the README. |
| C3 | **Two ledger renderers.** `scientific.js` owns `renderHistory()`, but `app.js:457 renderLedger()` checks for `app.renderHistory`, which is never assigned anywhere, so it falls back to its own `historyRow()`/rebuild. The two agree today (same class names, same newest-first order, same `data-index`), so the harness's `#history-list li.history__row` count stays 1 — but the markup is duplicated in two places. | confirm the row count stays 1 across commit → restore → clear in a browser, then wire `app.renderHistory = scientific renderHistory` or delete the fallback. |
| C4 | **The sparkline is invisible at 360 px** (`.spark { display: none }` at `max-width: 400px`). Assertions read the `points` attribute so they still pass, but the small-viewport screenshot lacks the visualisation. | intentional? if not, show a 60 px spark or a compact dot strip under 400 px. |
| C5 | *(checked, not a defect)* the graph canvas could have had a 0×0 backing store while `display:none`, but `graph.js` guards with `metrics()` returning `null` plus a `MutationObserver` on `body[data-mode]` and a `ResizeObserver` on `#plot`. | no action; noted so nobody "fixes" it twice. |

### D. Documentation defect

| # | Defect |
| --- | --- |
| D1 | `project_learnings.md` says "`#keypad` (23 `.key` buttons, each `data-key="…"`)". The shipped markup has **35** `.key` buttons inside `#keypad` (12 function keys + 23 pad keys); the 23-entry list in that document is the *pad* vocabulary, not the keypad size. Corrected in `project_learnings.md` by this task. |

---

## 4. Harness check → status map

| `verify_preview.py` check | Status here |
| --- | --- |
| no console errors / no uncaught page errors | **UNRUN** (no engine) |
| no external/CDN requests | static PASS (no remote `src`/`href`, no remote `url()`/`@import`, no `http://` in JS); browser-side unrun |
